recreation_brief:
1. Set the slide background to white (#FFFFFF), then draw a full-slide light-gray (#D6D6D6) rectangle covering 0%-100% of width and height; this gray rectangle is the visible frame/backdrop.
2. Draw a thin dark-red (#C00000) rectangle outline (no fill) inset ~4% from each slide edge as the outer border.
3. Place the slide title: centered bold red (#C00000) serif text 'Regression – One Dimensional Case' (~24-28pt) in the band ~2%-12% height and ~20%-80% width.
4. Draw the slide-number badge shape at top right (~88%-94% width, ~8%-14% height): a small horizontal oval with pale-yellow (#FFFFCC) fill and a thin red (#C00000) outline.
5. Type the numeral '3' in red (#C00000), centered inside the badge oval.
6. Draw the chart panel: a white (#FFFFFF) rectangle with a thin dark-red (#C00000) border, covering ~8%-92% of slide width and ~15%-97% of slide height.
7. Place the chart title inside the panel: centered bold dark-blue (#0000CC) serif text 'Length and Weight of  different samples of Steel Bars' (~20pt; keep the double space between 'of' and 'different') at ~20%-26% slide height.
8. Draw the y-axis: a thin red (#C00000) vertical line with a solid triangular arrowhead pointing up, along the panel's left edge, spanning ~18%-88% height.
9. Place the red (#C00000) label 'Weight' (~10-12pt), rotated 90° counterclockwise, at the top-left of the y-axis arrow.
10. Draw the x-axis: a thin red (#C00000) horizontal line with a solid triangular arrowhead pointing right, along the panel bottom at ~88% height, spanning ~12%-70% width. Do not add tick marks, numeric labels, gridlines, or a legend anywhere in the chart.
11. Place the red (#C00000) label 'Length' (~10-12pt) just below the right end of the x-axis arrow.
12. Plot exactly 23 circular scatter markers — orange (#E87D1E) fill, darker orange (#B85C00) outline, ~8-10px diameter — at these fractional plot positions (x from left, y from bottom): (0.22,0.18), (0.26,0.15), (0.30,0.22), (0.32,0.17), (0.35,0.16), (0.38,0.17), (0.42,0.24), (0.44,0.29), (0.45,0.25), (0.48,0.27), (0.49,0.31), (0.54,0.26), (0.55,0.34), (0.60,0.35), (0.61,0.36), (0.67,0.35), (0.73,0.42), (0.75,0.50), (0.83,0.49), (0.84,0.54), (0.89,0.54), (0.90,0.64), (0.95,0.67); the markers must form a positive linear trend from lower-left to upper-right.
13. From the highlighted marker at (0.75,0.50), draw two thin red (#C00000) dotted lines: one horizontal to the y-axis and one vertical down to the x-axis.
14. From the highlighted marker at (0.67,0.35), draw two thin red (#C00000) dotted lines: one horizontal to the y-axis and one vertical down to the x-axis.
15. Add a small red (#C00000) arrowhead marker on the y-axis at height ~0.50, aligned with the upper highlighted point's horizontal projection line.
16. Overlay a white mouse-pointer cursor arrow with black outline at plot position ~(0.89,0.60), next to the topmost points, to match the captured demonstration state.
17. Use a serif font (Times New Roman-like) for all text and keep every string verbatim: 'Regression – One Dimensional Case', 'Length and Weight of  different samples of Steel Bars', 'Weight', 'Length', '3'.
